i_was_swept_in: STATED PLAINLY, BECAUSE IT IS RULE 17'S PATHOLOGY AND IT HAPPENED TO ME WHILE I WAS OBEYING RULE 17. I finished, found .git/index.lock held by another agent, and waited 15 polls (~3.5 min) for the index to clear rather than forcing it — precisely so I would not stage a neighbour's 38 staged files into my commit. In that window three separate blanket commits banked my work under other agents' messages: the verdict, its JSON and this status file in f291b01 ('Bank: the canon comment correction and in-flight work'), tools/world/critic-w1-04-r3a.mjs in 770ca73, critic-w1-04-r3b.mjs in 692b6aa, and every screenshot in 377c26e. The blog line is in HEAD. NOTHING IS LOST and every file's content is the content I wrote — I verified each path against git log and the working tree is clean for all of them. But the attribution is wrong on all four, and this is now the FIFTH time the pattern is on record for this piece alone (round 1 logged it, round 2 logged it, round 3 logged doing it to two neighbours, and it has now happened twice more to me). The rule as written tells a finishing agent to stage by name; it does not tell a WAITING agent how to protect finished work from a neighbour's blanket add, and waiting politely is what exposed me. Worth a rule.
